bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Macro slowdown in Karnataka/Kerala/Telangana impacting non-steel demand; steel price volatility; execution risk in manufacturing turnaround; delayed Buildpro listing; competition in e-commerce and retail distribution
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and focused; clear strategic separation between entities; optimistic on manufacturing turnaround with new leadership and capex; bullish on Buildpro’s listing and non-steel growth; transparent on one-offs and guidance revisions
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Manufacturing business will now receive INR 5cr in 6-month rental income from Buildpro (from Oct 2025), improving its cash flow despite low EBITDA; Buildpro’s working capital cycle is only 27 days, enabling high ROCE (28-30%); 90% of Buildpro’s volume is steel, yet margins are improving despite steel’s low margin profile due to mix shift
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Pan-India processing footprint of 14 locations across 5 states, with dedicated facilities for tubes/strips (Bengaluru, Hyderabad) and roofing products (10 cities including Chennai, Coimbatore and Pune).
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Market/demand cyclicality — Operates in a highly competitive steel industry subject to economic cycles; demand is closely linked to overall economic activity in construction, infrastructure and automotive end-use sectors, and any slowdown can reduce consumption, sales volumes and lead to inventory accumulation. Government policy changes (import duties, export restrictions, environmental regulations) can also affect the operating environment.
- Steel price volatility / margin risk — Company is significantly exposed to fluctuations in steel prices driven by global supply-demand dynamics, raw material costs and macroeconomic conditions; adverse price movements can directly and materially impact operating margins and profitability.
- Inventory management risk — Steel manufacturing requires careful production planning and inventory management — holding high inventory during price declines can cause inventory losses, while insufficient inventory during price increases can cause missed revenue opportunities.
- Financial/leverage risk — Steel manufacturing operations are capital intensive, requiring significant investment in machinery and working capital; the Company is exposed to risks from its capital structure, funding requirements and reliance on external borrowings, with rising interest rates or tighter credit conditions raising finance costs and impacting profitability and cash flows.
- Working capital / receivables risk — Company must maintain inventories and extend credit to customers; delays in receivables or a slowdown in collections can impact liquidity and the ability to meet short-term obligations.
- Customer concentration / order-flow risk — A significant portion of revenue comes from a broad manufacturing customer base; loss of key customers, variations in customer demand, and changes in the timing/scale of customer procurement or capex cycles can cause fluctuations in operational and financial performance.
- Input cost & geopolitical/energy risk — Ongoing geopolitical conflicts (notably Middle East tensions and the Iran-U.S. conflict) have caused a cost-push impact on steel prices via sharp rises in coking coal, natural gas and oil costs (India is heavily import-dependent for energy), plus higher freight costs and delays from shipping-route disruptions.
- Emerging technology (AI) disruption — Management is evaluating the potential impact of the emergence of Artificial Intelligence on the business; preliminary assessment is that the impact will be negligible, but this is flagged as a watch item.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Post-demerger, Shankara Building Products Limited conducts the business of manufacturing and processing precision steel tubes, cold rolled strips, roofing profiles and accessories through three wholly owned subsidiaries. It sells entirely within the Indian domestic market to a customer base including automobile ancillary makers, white goods manufacturers, busbody builders and storage equipment manufacturers, alongside distributors, dealers and walk-in retail customers.

- **Roofing:** Colour coated roofing profiles, Decking sheets, Purlins, Rolling shutter patti

latest_quarter.body: Manufacturing EBITDA margin: 1% reported (Q2), 2% normalized (ex-INR 6cr one-time); targeting 2-2.5% in H2 FY26, 3% by H2 FY27; Non-steel margins: >6%; Steel margins: 3-3.5% avg (flat & roofing higher, pipes lower); Buildpro overall margin: 3.3% H1, targeting >3.5% in FY27 via non-steel mix and pricing stability
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: Buildpro 15-20%; Manufacturing ~10%; margin: Buildpro >3.5% by FY27; Manufacturing 2-2.5% in H2 FY26, targeting 3% by H2 FY27; order inflow: no specific guidance; capex/commissioning: INR 10-15cr in FY27 for machinery upgrades and finishing lines
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion into Maharashtra and Gujarat for non-steel; scaling e-commerce platform with new verticals; potential white-label product expansion beyond roofing (Ganga brand); demerger unlocks standalone valuation for marketplace business
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Post-demerger, sharper focus on the manufacturing business (precision steel tubes, cold rolled strips, roofing profiles) for better operational clarity and streamlined decision-making.
- Demerger strategically driven by Business Focus (separating trading and manufacturing verticals for sharper management attention) and Operational Clarity (simplifying reporting structures, improving accountability).
- Stronger emphasis on manufacture of niche products and better efficiency to improve overall quality of earnings post-demerger.
- Pursuing growth opportunities more aggressively, especially expanding the manufacturing footprint, enabled by reduced organisational complexity and enhanced management accountability.
- Board periodically reviews the Company's ability and need to distribute dividends with a view to preserving profitability and long-term growth plans; per its Dividend Distribution Policy, the Board decided it would be prudent not to recommend any dividend for FY26. The Dividend Distribution Policy was amended during the year to provide for declaration of dividend in years of exceptional gains or other events. No bonus shares, buyback, sweat equity or differential-rights shares were issued during the year, and paid-up capital was unchanged.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Post-demerger, management states the Company is positioned to pursue growth opportunities more aggressively, particularly in expanding its manufacturing footprint (precision steel tubes, cold rolled strips and roofing profiles), though no specific named project, site or commissioning timeline is disclosed in this bundle. On a standalone basis the Company incurred capital expenditure (gross) of ₹24.35 crores in FY26 versus ₹3.28 crores in FY25; on a consolidated basis, capex (gross) was ₹45.54 crores in FY26 versus ₹13.27 crores in FY25.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian steel industry growing at around 10% pace in FY26, driven by government policy (National Steel Policy targeting 300 million tonnes capacity by 2030, PLI scheme for specialty steel, PM Gati Shakti, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana).
- India has seen steady steel consumption growth of 8-10% over the last few years; precision steel tubes demand has grown over 15% on automobile, transport and storage/interiors growth, and the roofing segment is likewise growing over 15% on replacement of conventional roofing materials (cement, asbestos sheets) in industrial sheds and warehousing.
- Geopolitical conflict (Middle East, Iran-U.S. tensions) has had a cost-push impact on steel prices via higher coking coal, natural gas and oil costs and increased freight costs from shipping disruptions.
- FY27 outlook is a structural growth phase for India even as global steel markets undergo a cyclical recovery: India steel demand is expected to grow around 9.2% in FY27 (vs global growth of about 2.2%), supported by infrastructure spending, construction activity, automotive demand and capex cycles, and government programs (PM Gati Shakti, National Infrastructure Pipeline, housing, railway expansion).
- Despite global uncertainty from the Iran-U.S. conflict, management sees stable domestic demand for its products; the Company's entire production is sold in Indian markets.

deepdive.thesis: Shankara has successfully demerged its high-margin marketplace business (Buildpro) from its low-margin manufacturing arm, unlocking value through a near-term listing; the listed entity now focuses on manufacturing with a clear path to 3% EBITDA via capex, capacity utilization, and niche products, while Buildpro drives scalable growth with 15-20% revenue CAGR and margin expansion from non-steel mix.

A significant portion of revenue comes from a broad manufacturing customer base; loss of key customers, variations in customer demand, and changes in the timing/scale of customer procurement or capex cycles can cause fluctuations in operational and financial performance.

Ongoing geopolitical conflicts (notably Middle East tensions and the Iran-U.S. conflict) have caused a cost-push impact on steel prices via sharp rises in coking coal, natural gas and oil costs (India is heavily import-dependent for energy), plus higher freight costs and delays from shipping-route disruptions.

Management is evaluating the potential impact of the emergence of Artificial Intelligence on the business; preliminary assessment is that the impact will be negligible, but this is flagged as a watch item.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Shankara Building Products Limited is a manufacturer of precision steel tubes, cold rolled strips, roofing profiles and allied accessories, having demerged its omni-channel building-products marketplace business into a separate listed entity (Shankara Buildpro Limited) effective January 2026.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Post-demerger, Shankara Building Products Limited conducts the business of manufacturing and processing precision steel tubes, cold rolled strips, roofing profiles and accessories through three wholly owned subsidiaries. It sells entirely within the Indian domestic market to a customer base including automobile ancillary makers, white goods manufacturers, busbody builders and storage equipment manufacturers, alongside distributors, dealers and walk-in retail customers.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Vishal Precision Steel Tubes & Strips Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned (100%) material subsidiary; tube & cold rolled strip manufacturing/processing, registered office at Hoskote, Karnataka.
- Centurywells Roofing India Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned (100%) material subsidiary; colour-coated roofing products, registered office at Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu.
- Taurus Value Steel & Pipes Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned (100%) material subsidiary; steel pipes/tubes manufacturing and processing, registered office in Kutbullapur Mandal, Telangana.
- Steel Network (Holdings) Pte Limited, Singapore — subsidiary: Non-operating subsidiary domiciled in Singapore; wound up and liquidated with effect from December 26, 2025 (struck off).
- Shankara Buildpro Limited — related party: Formerly a wholly-owned subsidiary housing the Company's trading/marketplace business; ceased to be a subsidiary pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement (demerger), with listing completed in the first half of January 2026; remains a related party for RPT purposes (e.g. purchases/sales of goods during FY26).
- Shankara Holdings Private Limited, Bengaluru — related party: Named counterparty in the Company's related-party register; specific relationship category (relative/KMP-influence/control entity) is not unambiguously stated in this extracted text.
- Purple Splash Materials Private Limited, Bengaluru, Karnataka — related party: Named counterparty in the Company's related-party register; specific relationship category not unambiguously stated in this extracted text.
- The Café at Saanchi, Bengaluru — related party: Named counterparty in the Company's related-party register; specific relationship category not unambiguously stated in this extracted text.
- Shankara Building Products Employees Gratuity Fund, Bengaluru — related party: Employee gratuity trust fund of the Company, listed as a related party.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Steel: 90% of revenue; 60% pipes/tubes (30% growth), 20% flat products (60% growth), 15% roofing (30% growth), 5% longs (5% growth); Non-steel: 10-11% of revenue, growing at 10% YoY; Retail: 51% of revenue, Non-retail: 49%; E-commerce: INR 10cr H1, 250% YoY growth, EBITDA positive

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Tubes & Strips:** Precision steel tubes, Cold rolled (CR) strips, HR/CR/GP/GC flat steel products
- **Roofing:** Colour coated roofing profiles, Decking sheets, Purlins, Rolling shutter patti

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Automobile ancillaries
- White goods manufacturers
- Busbody builders
- Storage equipment manufacturers
- Distributors and dealers
- Walk-in retail customers
- Domestic India market only (nil exports)

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: Buildpro 15-20%; Manufacturing ~10%; margin: Buildpro >3.5% by FY27; Manufacturing 2-2.5% in H2 FY26, targeting 3% by H2 FY27; order inflow: no specific guidance; capex/commissioning: INR 10-15cr in FY27 for machinery upgrades and finishing lines

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into Maharashtra and Gujarat for non-steel; scaling e-commerce platform with new verticals; potential white-label product expansion beyond roofing (Ganga brand); demerger unlocks standalone valuation for marketplace business

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian steel industry growing at around 10% pace in FY26, driven by government policy (National Steel Policy targeting 300 million tonnes capacity by 2030, PLI scheme for specialty steel, PM Gati Shakti, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana).
- India has seen steady steel consumption growth of 8-10% over the last few years; precision steel tubes demand has grown over 15% on automobile, transport and storage/interiors growth, and the roofing segment is likewise growing over 15% on replacement of conventional roofing materials (cement, asbestos sheets) in industrial sheds and warehousing.
- Geopolitical conflict (Middle East, Iran-U.S. tensions) has had a cost-push impact on steel prices via higher coking coal, natural gas and oil costs and increased freight costs from shipping disruptions.
- FY27 outlook is a structural growth phase for India even as global steel markets undergo a cyclical recovery: India steel demand is expected to grow around 9.2% in FY27 (vs global growth of about 2.2%), supported by infrastructure spending, construction activity, automotive demand and capex cycles, and government programs (PM Gati Shakti, National Infrastructure Pipeline, housing, railway expansion).
- Despite global uncertainty from the Iran-U.S. conflict, management sees stable domestic demand for its products; the Company's entire production is sold in Indian markets.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Manufacturing EBITDA margin: 1% reported (Q2), 2% normalized (ex-INR 6cr one-time); targeting 2-2.5% in H2 FY26, 3% by H2 FY27; Non-steel margins: >6%; Steel margins: 3-3.5% avg (flat & roofing higher, pipes lower); Buildpro overall margin: 3.3% H1, targeting >3.5% in FY27 via non-steel mix and pricing stability

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Demerger completed; listing of Buildpro imminent (Nov 2025); capital allocation now split: Buildpro to fund retail/fulfillment expansion (5 stores, 3 FCs in FY27); Manufacturing to fund capex for margin improvement; no dividend or buyback guidance

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Post-demerger, management states the Company is positioned to pursue growth opportunities more aggressively, particularly in expanding its manufacturing footprint (precision steel tubes, cold rolled strips and roofing profiles), though no specific named project, site or commissioning timeline is disclosed in this bundle. On a standalone basis the Company incurred capital expenditure (gross) of ₹24.35 crores in FY26 versus ₹3.28 crores in FY25; on a consolidated basis, capex (gross) was ₹45.54 crores in FY26 versus ₹13.27 crores in FY25.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and focused; clear strategic separation between entities; optimistic on manufacturing turnaround with new leadership and capex; bullish on Buildpro’s listing and non-steel growth; transparent on one-offs and guidance revisions

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body: - Pan-India processing footprint of 14 locations across 5 states, with dedicated facilities for tubes/strips (Bengaluru, Hyderabad) and roofing products (10 cities including Chennai, Coimbatore and Pune).

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Macro slowdown in Karnataka/Kerala/Telangana impacting non-steel demand; steel price volatility; execution risk in manufacturing turnaround; delayed Buildpro listing; competition in e-commerce and retail distribution

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Manufacturing business will now receive INR 5cr in 6-month rental income from Buildpro (from Oct 2025), improving its cash flow despite low EBITDA; Buildpro’s working capital cycle is only 27 days, enabling high ROCE (28-30%); 90% of Buildpro’s volume is steel, yet margins are improving despite steel’s low margin profile due to mix shift

commitments.body:

|---|---|

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Post-demerger, sharper focus on the manufacturing business (precision steel tubes, cold rolled strips, roofing profiles) for better operational clarity and streamlined decision-making.
- Demerger strategically driven by Business Focus (separating trading and manufacturing verticals for sharper management attention) and Operational Clarity (simplifying reporting structures, improving accountability).
- Stronger emphasis on manufacture of niche products and better efficiency to improve overall quality of earnings post-demerger.
- Pursuing growth opportunities more aggressively, especially expanding …

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.
